facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 1986 near Linhai City in Zhejiang Province, China.
facts.quote: The fossil was discovered in 1986, near Linhai City in Zhejiang Province, China.

facts.statement: The genus was named after the Yandang mountains.
facts.quote: The genus was named after the Yandang mountains.

facts.statement: Yandangornis was the second primitive bird genus after Archaeopteryx found with a long, bony tail, a trait reflected in its specific name longicaudus meaning "long tail".
facts.quote: After Archaeopteryx, Yandangornis was the second genus of primitive bird found preserving a long, bony tail, and this trait was responsible for the specific name longicaudus, which is Latin for "long tail".

facts.statement: Features like blunt toe claws, a non-reversed hallux, and strong legs suggest a terrestrial mode of life.
facts.quote: Yandangornis had some features that suggest a terrestrial mode of life, such as blunt toe claws, a non-reversed hallux of the first toe, and strong legs.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest its terrestrial lifestyle may have evolved because its long, heavy tail would have inhibited flying ability.
facts.quote: This lifestyle may have evolved in response to the long, heavy tail of the genus, which would have inhibited flying ability.

facts.statement: Cai and Zhao originally classified Yandangornis in the monotypic family Yandangithidae and order Yandangithiformes within the subclass Sauriurae of the class Aves.
facts.quote: Cai and Zhao placed Yandangornis in a monotypic family (Yandangithidae) and order (Yandangithiformes) in the subclass Sauriurae of the class Aves.

facts.statement: Using recent definitions, Yandangornis is not considered a member of the class Aves because it is far more primitive than modern birds.
facts.quote: As Yandangornis was far more primitive than members of Aves, it is not considered a member of that class using recent definitions.

facts.statement: Zhou and Zhang (2007) noted that Yandangornis's affinities were poorly diagnosed and suggested it might be a non-avialan theropod.
facts.quote: Zhou and Zhang, 2007, briefly noted that Yandangornis's affinities were not sufficiently diagnosed, and that Yandangornis may potentially be a non-avialan genus of theropod.

facts.statement: Zhou and Zhang (2007) pointed out that Yandangornis's affinities were not sufficiently studied and that it could be a non-avian theropod genus.
facts.quote: Zhou y Zhang, 2007, señalaron que las afinidades de Yandangornis no fueron suficientemente estudiadas, y que Yandangornis podría ser un género de terópodos no aviarios.

facts.statement: Yandangornis is poorly documented in the literature and has been omitted from recent reevaluations of avialan systematics.
facts.quote: Yandangornis está poco documentado en la literatura, y el género se ha omitido en las revaluaciones recientes de la sistemática de Aviales.

facts.statement: The time range for Yandangornis is recorded as Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
